finding: In an onboarding run one agent reported commit d3618d2f06b52f02d54c593d47c4f29b510d58bd. The real commit was d3618d22d273577ebe702690c2449ca4cd91213f: the first seven characters match, the rest is invented. Two later agents reported correctly, so the fault is intermittent, and a spot check usually passes. In a related case an agent claimed it had verified every path it cited, yet one path pointed to tests/unit/ instead of tests/integration/. In automated mode dispatch verify-story already checks every reported SHA; work dispatched by hand has no such check. Fix: State in the dispatch contract that the parent checks every reported SHA with git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit} and git branch --contains, and that agents copy SHAs from git rev-parse output instead of typing them.
why_this_severity: `dispatch verify-story` checks every reported SHA in automated mode, so the contract works for dispatched work (no to fails_purpose). Work dispatched by hand has no such check, so a parent must spot an invented SHA itself.
